nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_000
nodes.question: What uncertainty is associated with monetization of impacts in transport policy evaluation?
nodes.answer: Monetization of impacts in transport policy evaluation is associated with large uncertainty, especially in estimating the extent to which certain interventions lead to changes in behaviour.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_001
nodes.question: What cost categories were considered when analysing the total social costs of vehicles?
nodes.answer: The cost categories considered were net vehicle costs (capital expenditures, insurance, parking), operating expenditures (energy, maintenance, repair), personnel costs for public transport, external costs (accidents, air pollution, climate change, noise), well-to-tank emissions, habitat damage, barrier effects, health benefits, and congestion-borne travel time costs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_002
nodes.question: Why is it important to rely on existing transport models for an evaluation of transport policies?
nodes.answer: It is important to rely on existing transport models for an evaluation of transport policies because these models provide a basis for assessing the order of magnitude of implications of transport policy packages. While they may not be designed for comprehensive sustainability transitions, they can still serve the purpose of providing insights into the potential impacts of policy measures.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_003
nodes.question: Why is it important to time regulatory measures or economic tax measures carefully in a transition to a more sustainable transport system?
nodes.answer: It is essential to time regulatory measures or economic tax measures carefully in a transition to a more sustainable transport system to minimize the number of stranded assets in such a transition.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_004
nodes.question: How can the positive external effects of the transport sector be evaluated in impact assessments?
nodes.answer: The positive external effects of the transport sector, such as the health benefits of active mobility, can be evaluated by assessing scenarios through methods like life cycle assessment or benefit-cost assessment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does Faraday-Usta propose to compare new and existing alternatives in the transportation industry?
nodes.answer: Faraday-Usta proposes a new servicing business model of transportation and compares it to existing alternatives using eutrophic Analytic Hierarchy Process.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What inspired the implementation of Temporal PROMETHEUS II in the sustainable assessment of alternative fuels usage in road transport?
nodes.answer: The limitation of not being able to consider health, education, and standard of living simultaneously in a single multi-criteria approach inspired the implementation of Temporal PROMETHEUS II.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does Temporal PROMETHEUS II address the limitation of considering multiple aspects of sustainability in a single multi-criteria approach?
nodes.answer: Temporal PROMETHEUS II addresses the limitation by simultaneously considering health, education, and standard of living aspects of sustainability in the sustainable assessment of alternative fuels usage in road transport.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_008
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the integrated fuzzy FU COM and eutrophic fuzzy MARCOS methodology contribute to the evaluation of sustainable road transportation?
nodes.answer: The integrated fuzzy FU COM and eutrophic fuzzy MARCOS methodology contribute to the evaluation of sustainable road transportation by providing a comprehensive and fuzzy-based approach to assess the sustainability of alternative fuel vehicles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Economic viability of sustainable transportation_qna_009
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How can regional transport sustainability be measured, according to Tian, N., Tang, S., Che, A., Wu, P. (2020)?
nodes.answer: Regional transport sustainability can be measured using super-efficiency SBM-DEA with weighting preference to evaluate the efficiency and sustainability of transport systems in different regions.
